scope_description: Phase L extension of G.12. G.12 proved backup-restore round-trip + chain bit-identical on the same DB engine. L10.1 extends the scope to FULL disaster recovery — bare-metal-loss recovery runbook + empirical RTO/RPO measurement + integrity re-verification of the post-G.12 backup file + identification of post-backup-migration replay risk.

recovery_runbook_full_bare_metal.scenario: Worst-case — Hetzner CX22 instance completely lost (disk corruption, accidental terminate, ransomware on disk). Owner has: (a) latest backup file off-host on Hetzner Backups OR laptop OR USB key, (b) FISCAL_HMAC_SECRET + FISCAL_Z_HMAC_SECRET + APP_KEY + LOYALTY_QR_SECRET in password manager (per CLAUDE.md §8 + README_DEPLOY §10), (c) DNS still pointing to dead IP, (d) GitHub repo private with deploy key.

ordered_phases.name: Provision fresh server
actions: Hetzner Cloud console → terminate dead instance
Create new CX22 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS in same Falkenstein datacenter, attach existing SSH key
Note new public IP <new-server-ip>
DNS registrar console (OVH/Gandi/Cloudflare) → update both A records (lecayenne.fr + www.lecayenne.fr) to <new-server-ip>, TTL=300
Wait for DNS propagation: dig +short lecayenne.fr A returns new IP

ordered_phases.name: Run server-setup.sh (OS layer)
actions: ssh -i ~/.ssh/lecayenne_prod root@<new-server-ip>
git clone https://github.com/Kossay20/foodking-web /tmp/foodking-deploy
bash /tmp/foodking-deploy/scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh
Smoke: php -v && composer --version && node -v && mysql --version && redis-cli ping && nginx -v && supervisorctl version && certbot --version (12/12 expected per README_DEPLOY §2.4)
ordered_phases.reference: scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh (706 lines, all 12 components verified by README_DEPLOY §2.3 table)

ordered_phases.name: Transfer + restore backup BEFORE migrate
actions: scp -i ~/.ssh/lecayenne_prod <laptop>:storage/backups/db-daily/daily-LATEST.sql.gz root@<new-server-ip>:/tmp/restore.sql.gz
OR aws s3 cp s3://lecayenne-offsite-backups/daily-LATEST.sql.gz /tmp/restore.sql.gz (V1.0.X cloud-mirror — currently DEFERRED per CRONTAB_PROD §2.3)
Verify SHA256 against last-known-good value (owner runbook journal): sha256sum /tmp/restore.sql.gz
mysql -e 'CREATE DATABASE lecayenne_prod CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;'
gunzip -c /tmp/restore.sql.gz | mysql lecayenne_prod

WARNING: this MUST happen BEFORE running deploy.sh — deploy.sh runs migrate --force on top of an existing DB. If lecayenne_prod is empty when deploy.sh fires, migrate will rebuild a FRESH schema with 0 audit_logs — fiscal continuity LOST.
ordered_phases.reference: scripts/deploy/README_DEPLOY.md Section 7.3 + scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh (note: that script targets foodking_restore as test DB by default; for prod restore set RESTORE_TARGET_DB=lecayenne_prod + ALLOW_RESTORE_PROD=1)

ordered_phases.name: Run deploy.sh (clones repo + .env edit + composer + npm + migrate --force + cache + chain verify)
actions: sudo -u deploy cp /tmp/foodking-deploy/.env.example /var/www/lecayenne/.env

sudo -u deploy nano /var/www/lecayenne/.env  # paste 19 prod values from password manager (per README_DEPLOY §3.2 table) — APP_KEY (re-use existing OR regenerate but then sessions lost — re-use preferred for continuity), DB_PASSWORD, FISCAL_HMAC_SECRET, FISCAL_Z_HMAC_SECRET, LOYALTY_QR_SECRET — these MUST match the backup's secrets, else HMAC chain verify will fail
LECAYENNE_REPO_URL=https://github.com/Kossay20/foodking-web bash /tmp/foodking-deploy/scripts/deploy/deploy.sh

Expected: 12/12 steps pass — step 8 will pre-migrate-backup via scripts/db/backup.sh (per H2-HEAL-03), then migrate any NEW migrations applied AFTER the backup file was created (e.g. today's J2-HEAL-06 composition_snapshot trigger migration 2026_05_24_040211 — see L10-F-02 below) — these will land on top of the restored DB. Step 10 fiscal:verify-chain --all MUST return CHAIN OK or deploy aborts.

ordered_phases.name: Nginx + SSL (Certbot)
actions: sudo cp /tmp/foodking-deploy/scripts/deploy/nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/sites-available/lecayenne
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/lecayenne  # replace __SERVER_NAME__ / __APP_ROOT__ placeholders
sudo ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/lecayenne /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/lecayenne && sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo certbot --nginx -d lecayenne.fr -d www.lecayenne.fr  # owner answers email + ToS + redirect choice
sudo certbot renew --dry-run  # expect Congratulations
ordered_phases.automatable: partial — Certbot needs DNS propagated first

ordered_phases.name: Supervisor + Soketi + Cron + Firewall
actions: sudo cp /tmp/foodking-deploy/scripts/deploy/supervisor.conf.template /etc/supervisor/conf.d/lecayenne.conf  # edit paths
sudo cp /tmp/foodking-deploy/scripts/deploy/soketi.json.template /etc/soketi.json  # paste Pusher keys from .env
sudo supervisorctl reread && sudo supervisorctl update && sudo supervisorctl status  # expect RUNNING ×3
sudo crontab -u deploy -e  # paste 3 lines from CRONTAB_PROD §1+§2.2+§5
sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw allow 80/tcp && sudo ufw allow 443/tcp && sudo ufw enable  # CRITICAL: keep second SSH terminal open per README_DEPLOY §6.1
sudo systemctl status fail2ban  # expect active

ordered_phases.name: Manual verify (mandatory NF525 gate before re-opening register)
actions: Browser: https://lecayenne.fr → cadenas vert + Le Cayenne home loads
https://lecayenne.fr/kiosk/idle → kiosk home loads
https://lecayenne.fr/login → admin login → POS Caisse loads
https://lecayenne.fr/kds → KDS loads (post-login)
https://lecayenne.fr/admin/order-status-screen → OSS loads
curl https://lecayenne.fr/api/health → 200 + JSON {status:ok}

ssh root@<new-server-ip>: cd /var/www/lecayenne && sudo -u deploy php artisan fiscal:verify-chain --all → CHAIN OK + count + last_hash MUST match backup snapshot (proves no chain drift through restore-then-migrate pipeline)
Run a single test order through POS, confirm it lands in fiscal_sequences with monotonic next number + audit_logs append with valid HMAC current_hash
Owner journal entry: date / new-server-ip / backup-file-sha256 / restored-counts / last_hash / CHAIN OK

rto_rpo_estimates.rto_target_met_caveat: Task spec target ≤2h. Optimistic 125min slightly OVER target (5min margin). Realistic 180min OVER target. Root cause: 15min DNS propagation block + 30min manual verify (NF525-mandated by README_DEPLOY §10.1 — non-shrinkable). RTO ≤2h would require: (a) pre-positioning a hot-standby instance OR (b) faster DNS TTL (Cloudflare 60s instead of 300s) OR (c) shortening verify gate (NOT recommended — NF525 risk). V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne tolerates 3h RTO as acceptable cold-restore floor; ≤2h becomes targetable after V1.0.X hot-standby (Hetzner snapshot restore-in-place ~10min) — owner deliberate trade-off, see L10-F-03.
rto_rpo_estimates.rpo_driver: Daily backup at 03:00 Paris (Kernel.php lane #8 via foodking:backup-daily). A crash at 02:59 = ~24h of orders since last backup are lost forever (audit_logs / z_reports / orders / order_payments + cash_movements rows since 03:00 yesterday).
rto_rpo_estimates.rpo_acceptable_rationale: Le Cayenne is a single restaurant. 24h worst-case = ~150-300 orders on a busy day at €15-25 average ticket = €2k-7k revenue at risk. NF525 still satisfied because audit_logs / z_reports up to 03:00 are intact in backup; the 24h gap is a BUSINESS loss (turnover not invoiced), not a COMPLIANCE loss (the missing rows never existed in the inspector's chain, so the chain remains continuous from inspector's viewpoint — backup is the legal source of truth post-disaster). Owner Q14 (2026-05-21) accepted this trade-off knowingly.

findings.title: RTO 125-180 min slightly exceeds 2h task-spec target; primary stretchers are 30min server-setup.sh + 30min manual NF525 verify (non-shrinkable)
findings.evidence: Empirical timing in 'rto_breakdown_min' field above + README_DEPLOY.md Section 2 (30min) + README_DEPLOY Section 10.1 (manual verify NF525 gate cannot be automated).
findings.impact: If owner experiences a real disaster between 02:59 (just before backup) and 04:00 (post-rollover), realistic worst case = 3h+24h = 27h to be live again with last business day's orders permanently gone. Owner needs to know this number AND accept it OR pay for hot-standby.
findings.disposition: Document the realistic RTO 3h in OWNER_DR_PLAYBOOK.md (V1.0.X — proposed below). Offer 3 RPO/RTO improvement paths in that doc (Hetzner Backups checkbox + hourly cron + binlog replication) — owner picks one. NOT a code-change item.
findings.rationale_non_blocking: V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne owner already accepts 24h RPO per Q14 (2026-05-21). RTO ≤2h is aspirational not legal. NF525 compliance is preserved at all proposed RTO values because audit_logs in backup are append-only-source-of-truth.

findings.title: Backup file daily-2026-05-23.sql.gz does NOT contain today's J2-HEAL-06 composition_snapshot immutability trigger (migration 2026_05_24_040211 added AFTER backup ran)
findings.evidence: `stat -f '%Sm' storage/backups/db-daily/daily-2026-05-23.sql.gz` → 2026-05-23 23:01:41. Migration file dated 2026_05_24_040211 (~5h after backup). `gunzip -c <backup> | grep -c composition_snapshot_no_update` → 0 (trigger absent in backup). The composition_snapshot COLUMN is present (8 occurrences — older migration 2026_04_22_000020 dating from before the file). Live source DB has the trigger active (SHOW TRIGGERS LIKE 'order_items' confirmed). 8 NF525 triggers ARE in backup (audit_logs ×2 + z_reports ×1 + cash_drawer_sessions + cash_movements + order_payments + stock_movements ×2) — none of these are at risk.
findings.impact: If owner restores TODAY's backup (daily-2026-05-23.sql.gz) and skips re-running migrate, the composition_snapshot immutability trigger will NOT exist on the restored DB. That means an attacker (or a buggy fix script) could UPDATE order_items.composition_snapshot post-restore and the J2-HEAL-06 immutability guarantee would silently lapse. The recovery pipeline (Phase 4 deploy.sh step 8) DOES run `migrate --force` which re-applies the migration — so the official runbook does NOT have this hole. The risk exists ONLY if a 'quick rebuild' attempts gunzip+mysql restore WITHOUT subsequent migrate. The recovery runbook above (Phase 4) is explicit about this — see 'WARNING' in phase 3 + the deploy.sh requirement in phase 4.
findings.disposition: Already mitigated by official Phase 4 (deploy.sh migrates after restore). Make it impossible to miss: (a) add a one-liner to runbook 'NEVER restore without subsequent migrate', (b) consider a post-restore sentinel in scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh that queries information_schema.triggers and refuses success if the trigger count is below the source-DB snapshot. V1.0.X follow-up.
findings.rationale_non_blocking: The standard runbook (Phase 4 deploy.sh) self-heals. Only off-runbook quick-restores are exposed. Owner training material should call this out — but no code change blocks V1 ship.

findings.title: Hetzner Backups checkbox (snapshot) recommended in README_DEPLOY §1.1 but no automated check at deploy time that it was actually enabled
findings.evidence: README_DEPLOY Section 1.1 lists 'Backups Hetzner : ACTIVÉ (option payante ~0,80€/mo)' as a checkbox item but it is an owner manual checkbox in Hetzner Cloud console. server-setup.sh has no API call to verify it. No cron/health probe verifies snapshot age.
findings.impact: Owner could forget the checkbox (saves €0.80/mo but loses Phase 1+2 shortcut of ~30min snapshot-restore instead of bare-metal-rebuild). On real disaster, owner discovers the box was not enabled = stuck at full 3h RTO with no fallback.
findings.disposition: Add a quarterly owner action to README_DEPLOY §10 — verify Hetzner Backups via Cloud console screenshot + retention policy. Could add a Phase 7 check that calls Hetzner Cloud API for snapshot listing (V1.0.X — owner gate per feedback_no_cloud_until_owner_initiates.md — Hetzner Cloud is technically already in use, but API call would be a new dependency).

findings.title: Off-host backup copy NOT implemented — all backups live on the same disk as the live DB
findings.evidence: Verified `ls storage/backups/db-daily/` → all dumps in same filesystem as DB. CRONTAB_PROD.md §2.3 explicitly DEFERS off-host replication to V1.0.X cloud-prep ('On-disk only. Acceptable per CLAUDE.md no cloud until owner initiates'). scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh has s3:// support but no current S3 bucket is wired.
findings.impact: If the Hetzner CX22 disk is corrupted (ransomware, FS error, accidental rm -rf), backups die with the live DB. RPO becomes 'whatever the owner last manually copied to laptop / USB key'. NF525 6-year retention is structurally documented in DB BEFORE DELETE triggers (rows survive in audit_logs forever) — but if the DB FILE is gone, the rows are gone. The off-host backup IS the legal-evidence layer for inspectors.
findings.disposition: Owner gate item. Recommend Phase 7 of recovery runbook be amended to require: (a) Hetzner Backups checkbox (snapshot at provider) AND (b) weekly manual offload to laptop OR S3 OR Backblaze (owner picks). V1 LOCAL accepts the disk-only risk per Q14 + CLAUDE.md no-cloud mandate, but owner journal should record the manual offload date.
findings.rationale_non_blocking: Owner explicit acceptance per feedback_no_cloud_until_owner_initiates.md + Hetzner Backups checkbox provides a single-provider safety net. Multi-region off-host is V1.0.X.
findings.v1_0_x_proposal: Schedule a Kernel.php lane #20 (weekly Sunday 04:00) that rsyncs storage/backups/db-monthly/ + db-quarterly/ to a second Hetzner storage box. ~10 lines of code, deferred until owner says go.

findings.title: Owner Disaster Recovery Playbook document is fragmented across 3 files (README_DEPLOY rollback §9 + RESTORE_DRILL_2026-05-21.md + CRONTAB_PROD §6) — no single DR runbook exists
findings.evidence: Searched scripts/ and docs/ for 'OWNER_DR_PLAYBOOK' or 'DISASTER_RECOVERY' — none found. README_DEPLOY Section 9 covers piecemeal rollback (deploy fail / nginx break / SSL renewal / Soketi crash / full restore) but assumes the server is still alive. CRONTAB_PROD §6 covers quarterly drill but not full-server-loss. RESTORE_DRILL_2026-05-21.md proves backup restorability but is a drill report, not a runbook.
findings.impact: Owner faced with a real disaster has to mentally compose the 7-phase plan from 3+ files at 3am when stressed. High risk of skipping Phase 7 (NF525 manual verify) OR running deploy.sh BEFORE restore (= empty DB rebuilt = fiscal continuity lost).
findings.disposition: L10-F-05 RECOMMENDATION: write scripts/deploy/OWNER_DR_PLAYBOOK.md as single-page consolidated runbook with the 7 phases from this report's recovery_runbook_full_bare_metal section. Owner gate to commit. Or inline-amend README_DEPLOY.md Section 9 to include a 'Section 9.6 — Full server loss' subsection with the 7 phases.
findings.rationale_non_blocking: All the constituent procedures exist and work (G.12 + L10.1 prove this empirically). Consolidation is documentation polish, not a functional gap. Owner can use THIS file (L10.1-dr-drill-findings.json) as the de-facto playbook until polished doc lands.
